title: What is TSMC?
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) is the world's largest semiconductor manufacturer, producing chips for major tech companies like Apple, Amazon, and Google. It focuses solely on manufacturing for third parties, unlike competitors, and boasts significant market dominance and advanced process technology. The article also discusses the potential impact of a Chinese invasion of Taiwan on TSMC and its global operations, as well as the company's expansion plans in the US.

title: Apple’s market value drops below $2 trillion
summary: Apple Inc.'s market capitalization fell below $2 trillion for the first time since March 2021, driven by concerns over high inflation and a slowing global economy impacting demand for its products. This significant drop follows a year after the company briefly reached a $3 trillion valuation. Analysts have downgraded Apple due to anticipated supply chain issues and reduced consumer spending on high-end phones, forecasting a potential revenue decline.

title: If You Invested $100 in Berkshire Hathaway in 1965, This Is How Much You Would Have Today
summary: If an investor had put $100 into Berkshire Hathaway in 1965, that investment would be valued at approximately $2.42 million today, representing a 2,419,900% return. This significantly outperforms a similar investment in the S&P 500, which would be worth about $22,400. The article highlights Berkshire's history under Warren Buffett, its strategic diversification into various sectors including insurance and tech (like Apple), and its consistent market-beating performance.

title: If You Invested $100 in Berkshire Hathaway in 1965, This Is How Much You Would Have Today
summary: This article illustrates the phenomenal returns of investing in Berkshire Hathaway since Warren Buffett took over in 1965. A $100 investment made then would be worth approximately $2.42 million today, significantly outperforming the S&P 500. The article details Berkshire's strategic shift from textiles to insurance, its acquisitions like GEICO and Burlington Northern Santa Fe, and its current diverse portfolio including a significant stake in Apple.

title: Foxconn to use Nvidia chips to build self-driving vehicle platforms
summary: Electronics manufacturer Foxconn and chipmaker Nvidia Corp have partnered to develop autonomous vehicle platforms. Foxconn will manufacture electronic control units (ECUs) based on Nvidia's DRIVE Orin chip for self-driving cars, aiming to address challenges in the global automotive market. Nvidia views this collaboration as a way to scale its efforts and meet the increasing demand for chips in autonomous and connected vehicles, projecting a $300 billion market opportunity in the automotive sector.

title: Tuesday's ETF with Unusual Volume: IWL
summary: The iShares Russell Top 200 ETF (IWL) experienced unusually high trading volume on Tuesday, with shares down about 0.8%. Tesla and Apple, major components of the ETF, saw significant trading volume and share price drops, while PayPal Holdings performed best, rising 4.3%.

title: Think you have it bad?
summary: The article discusses the tough economic environment of 2022, highlighting how general market downturns for stocks and bonds meant financial advisors and fund managers who weren't down 20% effectively "won." It then focuses on two specific groups particularly affected: tech startup employees facing worthless stock options and layoffs, and mortgage brokers and realtors experiencing a deep freeze in the housing market after a period of rapid growth. The author suggests empathy for these groups, acknowledging the widespread difficulties while offering his firm's services for financial planning.

title: Salesforce to lay off 10% of workforce to cut costs amid economic downturn
summary: Salesforce announced it will lay off 10% of its workforce and reduce office space to cut operating costs amid a challenging economic environment. CEO Marc Benioff admitted the company "hired too many people" during the pandemic's revenue surge, and the company is now facing the consequences. This move follows similar cost-cutting measures by other tech giants like Amazon, Apple, and Meta Platforms.

title: Apple to sign Luxshare for iPhone production in China - FT
summary: Apple is reportedly set to partner with Chinese contract manufacturer Luxshare Precision Industry Co Ltd for the production of premium iPhone models. Luxshare has already been producing a small number of iPhone 14 Pro Max models to address production shortfalls at Foxconn's Zhengzhou factory last year. This move is seen as Apple's strategy to diversify its supplier base following production disruptions caused by employee unrest and COVID-19 lockdowns in China.

title: Apple brings AI narration to audiobooks
summary: Apple Inc. has introduced AI-narrated audiobooks through Apple Books, utilizing text-to-speech technology to make audiobook production more accessible and affordable for publishers and authors. While the digital voices aim to reduce costs and complexity, some critics note an "artificial edge" compared to human narrators. Apple plans to improve the AI voices and currently offers them for select English-language romance and fiction books, with more voices and nonfiction categories in development.

title: Android has a response to iPhone’s satellite connection, thanks to Qualcomm
summary: Qualcomm is introducing Snapdragon Satellite service, a new emergency satellite phone service for Android smartphones. This service aims to compete with Apple's existing satellite connectivity, with specific product announcements expected by mid-year. The service requires at least one ground gateway to connect smartphones to satellites.

title: Nordstrom appoints Atticus Tysen to its board of directors
summary: Nordstrom, Inc. has announced the appointment of Atticus Tysen to its board of directors, effective January 3, 2023. Tysen brings over three decades of engineering and information security experience, currently serving as senior vice president of product development, chief information security, and fraud prevention officer for Intuit. His expertise is expected to enhance the board's focus on technology and cybersecurity within the retail industry.

title: Qualcomm partners with Iridium to develop satellite connectivity
summary: Qualcomm has announced a partnership with Iridium to launch Snapdragon Satellite, bringing satellite connectivity to next-generation premium Android phones and other devices. This service will enable global mobile messaging and emergency services in areas without traditional coverage. Other companies like Apple, Bullitt Group, T-Mobile with SpaceX, BICS with Lynk, AST SpaceMobile, and Huawei are also actively developing their own satellite connectivity solutions, highlighting a growing race for space-based mobile communication.

title: Apple Analyst Says BOE Will Become Largest Display Supplier for iPhone 15
summary: An Apple analyst in Taiwan predicts that China's BOE will become the largest display supplier for Apple's iPhone 15 series, significantly surpassing Samsung Display. BOE is expected to supply around 70% of OLED panels for the iPhone 15 and 15 Plus, and potentially 20-30% of LTPO panels for the iPhone 16. This shift indicates a growing challenge from Chinese companies to Korean dominance in the OLED display market.

title: Kartoon Channel! Expands Global Reach
summary: Kartoon Channel!, owned by Genius Brands International, has expanded its global distribution through new partnerships. The channel is now available on Vizio smart TVs in North America and via in-flight entertainment systems on several major airlines, including British Airways and Qatar Airways. This expansion aligns with Kartoon Channel!'s strategy to diversify its business model and reach more viewers worldwide.

title: Garmin Venu Sq2 Review | A fitness lifestyle companion
summary: The Garmin Venu Sq2 is reviewed as a robust fitness lifestyle companion that boasts impressive battery life, lasting over a week on a single charge. The review highlights its advanced health tracking features, accurate GPS, AMOLED display, and subscription-free breathing exercises, making it suitable for those pursuing new fitness goals despite its cost. The article details its performance across various activities including running, HIIT, Pilates, swimming, and even scuba diving, affirming its versatility and improvement over its predecessor.

title: You might actually want a TiVo TV someday
summary: Xperi, the company that owns the TiVo brand, is launching its own TiVo OS smart TV platform in Europe in the first half of 2023, with U.S. availability planned for the future. The platform focuses on content discovery over apps, offering recommendations across various streaming services and an intuitive voice search. While it currently lacks a robust app store compared to competitors, its neutral approach and potential for ad revenue sharing aim to attract TV manufacturers.

title: U.S. Supreme Court lets Meta's WhatsApp pursue 'Pegasus' spyware suit
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court has allowed Meta Platforms Inc's WhatsApp to proceed with a lawsuit against Israel's NSO Group. WhatsApp accuses NSO Group of exploiting a bug in its messaging app to install "Pegasus" spyware, enabling the surveillance of 1,400 individuals, including journalists and human rights activists. NSO Group had argued for immunity, claiming it acted as an agent for foreign governments, but the Supreme Court rejected their appeal.

title: Inari’s share price down over 4% as Apple plans to drop Broadcom chip from devices
summary: Inari Amertron Bhd's share price dropped over 4% after reports that Apple plans to replace Broadcom's Wi-Fi and Bluetooth chips with in-house designs by 2025. Although Inari's exposure to Broadcom is mainly on complex RF chips, which are harder to replace in the short term, the news still impacted the company's stock given its significant reliance on Broadcom. Apple is Broadcom's largest customer, accounting for about 20% of its revenue, and Inari is heavily dependent on Broadcom.

title: Illumina, the DNA sequencing giant, gives Wall Street bad news
summary: Illumina, the world's largest maker of DNA sequencing technology, has delivered disappointing news to investors, announcing a lower profit outlook for 2023. The company, which has successfully driven down the cost of sequencing a human genome, is now facing challenges due to its own success and uncertainties in funding for genetic research. Consequently, Illumina's stock price has significantly dropped from its peak in 2021.

title: Pepsi, Coke soda pricing targeted in new federal probe
summary: The Federal Trade Commission has launched a preliminary investigation into Coca-Cola and PepsiCo's pricing strategies for potential price discrimination in the soft drink market. This probe revives the largely dormant Robinson-Patman Act of 1936, which prohibits suppliers from offering better prices to large retailers over smaller competitors. The investigation signals the Biden administration's broader effort to apply antitrust scrutiny beyond the tech sector to traditional large companies.

title: Apple to start using in-house screens from 2024 - Bloomberg News
summary: Apple plans to begin using its own custom displays in mobile devices starting in 2024, aiming to reduce reliance on external suppliers like Samsung and LG. The transition will start with high-end Apple Watches, followed by other devices including the iPhone, and will involve upgrading to microLED technology. This move is part of a broader strategy by Apple to bring more component production in-house, following similar shifts with chips from Broadcom and Intel.

title: Inari pares loss as analysts see limited impact from Apple's plan to drop Broadcom chip
summary: Inari Amertron Bhd shares recovered some losses after analysts indicated that Apple's plan to replace Broadcom chips with in-house designs would have a limited impact on Inari's outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) business. Analysts noted Inari's direct exposure to Apple's revenue through Broadcom is relatively small (17-18%) and that Inari's involvement in complex RF filters is unlikely to be immediately affected. Despite a maintained "market perform" rating with a slightly reduced target price, some analysts suggest the negative news is already priced in, presenting a potential buying opportunity.

title: Apple Watch patent infringement finding; Masimo seeks import ban
summary: A US court has ruled that Apple infringed on one of Masimo's pulse oximeter patents with its Apple Watch Series 6 and up, a significant setback in their ongoing legal battle. Masimo is now seeking a US import ban on all current Apple Watches, which could halt sales in the country. The United States International Trade Commission (USITC) will determine whether to implement this import ban.

title: Apple debuts free tool to help businesses get noticed
summary: Apple has launched a new free online tool called Apple Business Connect, designed to help businesses customize their information cards in Apple Maps and other services. This allows businesses to update details like hours, add photos, promote limited-time offers, and access analytics. The initiative aims to provide useful local information and potentially attract more engagement from merchants and consumers.

title: Kuo doubles down on iPhone 15 Pro having no physical buttons
summary: Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo has reiterated his claim that the iPhone 15 Pro will feature solid-state buttons instead of physical ones, similar to the iPhone SE 2's home button. His latest survey indicates that Cirrus Logic will be the exclusive supplier of the Taptic Engine's controller IC for this change. Kuo also predicts that if users respond positively, this technology may be adopted in other high-end models in the future, alongside rumors of a rounded, titanium chassis for the iPhone 15 range.

title: Back Again At Comparing Skyworks Vs. Qorvo (NASDAQ:SWKS)
summary: This article compares Skyworks Solutions and Qorvo, both RF suppliers currently trading at low P/E ratios. It highlights Qorvo's transparency regarding market details and Skyworks' stable growth due to its strong ties with Apple. The author also suggests Qorvo has a significant opportunity with Apple's business, especially given Qualcomm's apparent withdrawal.

title: IDC, Gartner: 2022 PC Demand Dropped To Its ‘Lowest Level In Years’
summary: PC demand in 2022 dropped significantly to its lowest level in years, according to reports from IDC and Gartner. This decline was attributed to global recession, inflation, higher interest rates, and consumers already owning newer PCs purchased during the pandemic. The business market too saw a decline as enterprise buyers extended PC life cycles and delayed purchases, with growth not expected until 2024.

title: Meta faces a future of more legal woes and falling revenues
summary: Meta, formerly Facebook, is experiencing significant challenges including plummeting stock value, falling revenues, and increasing regulatory scrutiny, a situation that worsened after its rebrand in October 2021. Despite investor concerns and substantial losses from its metaverse division, Reality Labs, CEO Mark Zuckerberg remains committed to heavy investment in the metaverse. The company also faces ongoing legal battles, hefty fines for data privacy breaches, and a class-action lawsuit settlement, exacerbating doubts about its future prospects.

title: Starbucks tells corporate employees to return to the office
summary: Starbucks is requiring its corporate employees to return to the office for a minimum of three days a week, with specific days designated for in-person collaboration. Interim CEO Howard Schultz stated in a memo that the policy, effective January 30, aims to rebuild company culture, foster human connection, and ensure fairness among employees, especially considering store and plant workers who could not work remotely. This move aligns Starbucks with other companies like Disney and Apple that have also implemented stricter return-to-office mandates.

title: Buffett-Backed Taiwan Semiconductor Braces for Chip-Sector Downturn
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) reported record profits for its fourth quarter, exceeding analyst expectations, but also issued a warning about a potential downturn in demand for 2023. This news comes as the company, backed by Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway, indicates higher costs for building facilities in the U.S. compared to Taiwan. TSMC is preparing for a challenging period in the chip sector despite its strong recent financial performance.

title: Starbucks tells corporate employees to return to office 3 days a week
summary: Starbucks is requiring corporate employees to return to the office three days a week by the end of January, a move announced by interim CEO Howard Schultz. This decision comes as other major companies like Disney, Apple, and Snapchat's parent company are also enforcing stricter return-to-office policies, with some citing low compliance with previous hybrid work arrangements. The shift reflects a broader trend of companies clamping down on remote work that became common during the Covid-19 pandemic.

title: Apple CEO Tim Cook to take more than 40% pay cut
summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook will receive a target total compensation of $49 million in 2023, marking a pay cut of over 40% from the previous year. This adjustment comes after Apple's compensation committee considered shareholder feedback on executive pay and a recommendation from Cook himself. While his base salary remains $3 million, equity awards have been restructured to align his compensation between the 80th and 90th percentiles relative to Apple's peer group.

title: Apple CEO Tim Cook to take a more than 40 percent pay cut
summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook is set to take a more than 40 percent pay cut in 2023, reducing his target compensation to $49 million, down from nearly $100 million in previous years. This adjustment was made due to shareholder feedback, the company's performance, and Cook's own recommendation. The compensation committee aimed to align his pay between the 80th and 90th percentiles relative to peer groups for future years.

title: Oracle jumps into payments for retailers
summary: Oracle has expanded its services for retailers to include in-store payment acceptance, offering tap-to-pay capabilities for various payment methods like debit, credit, Apple, Google, and Samsung digital wallets. This new feature, which became available in December, will be sold at a fixed fee without long-term contracts or minimum monthly payment volumes. Oracle aims to provide a more stable and cost-effective "payment to processing" solution, integrating it with their existing hardware and cloud-based software for inventory and staff management.

title: How Both Taiwan and the US Can Benefit from TSMC's Investment
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) is increasing its investment in the U.S. to $40 billion, building a second factory in Phoenix, Arizona. This move, supported by the CHIPS and Science Act, aims to strengthen the U.S. domestic semiconductor industry and diversify global supply chains. Experts suggest that while complete self-sufficiency for the U.S. might be unrealistic, this investment helps address critical dependencies, enhances national security, and fosters innovation in chip manufacturing.

title: Apple Takes Major Steps Toward ‘Owning’ Its Key Technology
summary: Apple (AAPL) is reportedly taking significant steps to assert greater control over its proprietary technology. This initiative involves increasingly developing its own in-house chips and custom displays. Such moves signify a strategic shift towards self-reliance and vertical integration within the company's product development.

title: From Apple To Amazon And Toyota, Here Are The Top 10 Biggest Companies In The World
summary: This article lists the top 10 biggest companies in the world based on revenue. Walmart, State Grid Corporation Of China, and Amazon lead the list, primarily highlighting a competition between US and Chinese firms. The article also includes companies from Japan and Germany, detailing their revenue, founding year, and number of employees.

title: Biometric Sensors Market Size to Touch USD 3.5829 million by 2030 According to Acumen Research and Consulting
summary: The global biometric sensors market is projected to grow from USD 1.3195 million in 2021 to USD 3.5829 million by 2030, exhibiting a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 11.9% from 2022 to 2030. This growth is driven by increasing demand for secure authentication, advancements in technology, and wider adoption in various sectors like healthcare, banking, and government. Despite its growth, the market faces challenges due to lack of standardization, high implementation costs, and privacy concerns.

title: Goldman Sachs Vs. Jefferies: Which Is the Better Investment?
summary: This article compares Goldman Sachs (GS) and Jefferies Financial Group (JEF) as investment opportunities, especially in light of Berkshire Hathaway's decision to exit its Goldman Sachs position and initiate a new, albeit small, position in Jefferies. The author highlights Jefferies' smaller size, focused strategy in investment banking, higher dividend yield, and lower valuation as potential advantages over the larger and more diversified Goldman Sachs, suggesting a rationale for Berkshire Hathaway's move. Though both firms are performing well, the piece implies Jefferies may have greater long-term growth potential.

title: TSMC expects revenue to fall amid declining chip demand
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) anticipates a decline in revenue for 2023 due to softening demand for chips, particularly from consumer device and data center clients. Despite a 26.7% year-over-year revenue increase in Q4, the company expects a more than 14% drop in Q1 revenue. TSMC forecasts the semiconductor market to bottom out in the first half of 2023, with a recovery expected in the second half, and is adjusting its spending plans accordingly while still investing in new facilities like the Arizona fab.

title: Temu Review: What Is Temu and Why Is It Suddenly America’s Most Popular App?
summary: Temu, the American sister brand of China's Pinduoduo, has rapidly become America's most popular shopping app since its U.S. launch last fall. Its success is primarily attributed to extremely low prices, free shipping, and aggressive advertising. While the author found good deals on certain electronics and kitchen items, he advises caution on other categories and notes the app's business model involves cutting out middlemen for direct sales.

title: Netflix’s Reed Hastings steps aside as co-CEO, stays on as executive chairman
summary: Netflix co-founder Reed Hastings has stepped down as co-CEO, transitioning to executive chairman, with COO Greg Peters joining Ted Sarandos as co-CEO. This leadership change comes as Netflix aims to reaccelerate growth amid increased competition and a slowdown in subscriber numbers. The company reported slower fourth-quarter revenue but exceeded subscriber expectations, attributing success to popular shows and new initiatives like an ad-supported plan and paid password sharing.

title: Global X S&p 500 Covered Call Etf Share Price
summary: This article provides detailed financial information for the Global X S&P 500 Covered Call ETF (XYLD), including its current share price, performance metrics, historical returns, and fundamental data like expense ratio and AUM. It also lists the top holdings, sector breakdown, market cap distribution, and offers insights on its performance against peers and market cap movements. The article concludes with an FAQ section on investing in XYLD from India.

title: Apple’s Reliance On China Poses A Problem For The Company
summary: This article discusses Apple's significant reliance on its supply chain in China and the challenges this poses for the company amidst growing geopolitical tensions and trade barriers between the US and China. It highlights how Apple's deep integration with Chinese manufacturing, including specialized labor and R&D, makes disentanglement difficult, even as the US government increases pressure through tariffs, forced labor prevention acts, and technology export controls. The article suggests that while Apple is starting to move some operations, achieving true independence from China will be a slow and arduous process.

title: 予算3万円台の「スマートウォッチ」おすすめ5選　人気の「Apple Watch SE」から、コスパが良い高機能モデルまで【2023年1月版】 - Fav-Log by ITmedia
summary: This article recommends five smartwatches under 30,000 yen, including popular models like the Apple Watch SE and high-performance, cost-effective alternatives. It caters to users looking for smartwatches equipped with functions like health tracking, mobile payments, and sports activity monitoring. The selection includes devices suitable for various needs, from outdoor enthusiasts to those prioritizing design.

title: Silicon Valley 2.0? 5 US cities that could be the new tech start-up central
summary: Several southern US cities are emerging as new tech hubs, drawing companies like Tesla, Apple, Oracle, Microsoft, and Google away from California's Silicon Valley. High tax rates, labor costs, regulations, and a declining quality of life in Silicon Valley are pushing these companies to look for more affordable and business-friendly environments in states such as Texas, Arizona, Georgia, and Florida. These new tech centers offer incentives, lower costs of living, and new luxury residential developments to accommodate the influx of workers.

title: 7 Growth Stocks That Will Make You Rich in 10 Years
summary: This article identifies seven growth stocks across diverse high-demand sectors like technology, cybersecurity, nanotechnology, healthcare, and electric vehicles that are positioned to generate significant wealth for investors within the next decade. The selected companies, including Apple, Palo Alto Networks, Applied Materials, Intuitive Surgical, Welltower, ChargePoint, and Marathon Digital, are highlighted for their potential to capitalize on future market trends and innovation. Despite current market hesitations, the author emphasizes the long-term potential of these companies based on their strategic positioning and projected growth.

title: How Apple’s Upcoming Mixed-Reality Headset Will Work
summary: Apple's upcoming mixed-reality headset, likely named Reality Pro, is an ambitious attempt to create a 3D version of iOS with advanced eye and hand-tracking. Priced around $3,000, it aims to revolutionize virtual meetings and immersive video, challenging Meta Platforms Inc.'s dominance in the VR industry. This launch marks Apple's first major new product category since the Apple Watch in 2015, representing a significant strategic move for the company.

title: Nokia Corp. ADR rises Monday, still underperforms market
summary: Nokia Corp. ADR (NOK) saw a slight increase of 0.43% on Monday, closing at $4.63. Despite this rise, the stock underperformed the broader market, as both the NASDAQ Composite and Dow Jones Industrial Average rose more significantly. The gain broke a four-day losing streak for Nokia ADR, though it remained below its 52-week high and lagged behind competitors like BlackBerry Ltd., Apple Inc., and Motorola Solutions Inc.

title: Apple builds on privacy commitment by unveiling new education and awareness efforts on Data Privacy Day
summary: In celebration of Data Privacy Day, Apple has launched new educational resources to help users manage their data. These efforts include a "Today at Apple" session focusing on iPhone privacy features and a partnership with Nick Mohammed for a short film titled "A Day in the Life of an Average Person’s Data" to raise awareness. Apple emphasizes that privacy is a fundamental human right, built into all its products and services.

title: Nokia Corp. ADR underperforms Tuesday when compared to competitors
summary: Nokia Corp. ADR (NOK) dropped 1.73% to $4.55 on Tuesday, performing worse than many of its competitors, despite a mixed day for the broader stock market. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose while the NASDAQ Composite Index fell. Nokia's ADR closed significantly below its 52-week high, and its trading volume was higher than its 50-day average.

title: Choice Hotels Opens Cambria Hotel Austin Uptown Near the Domain
summary: Choice Hotels International has opened the Cambria Hotel Austin Uptown Near the Domain, marking its second property in Austin, Texas, with a third on the way. The 135-room hotel is strategically located in Austin's high-tech corridor, providing convenient access to major tech companies and local attractions. It offers modern amenities and design-forward accommodations aimed at both business and leisure travelers.

title: Goldman Sachs signals partial retreat from consumer banking
summary: Goldman Sachs is partially retreating from its consumer banking efforts after accumulating $3 billion in losses since 2020. The firm is scrapping plans for a checking account and winding down its personal loan business, Marcus, to refocus on its core investment banking and wealth management services. While a popular savings account and credit card business will continue, the losses in consumer lending have attracted regulatory scrutiny.

title: Big Tech to Congress: Listen to Taylor Swift and Go After Ticketmaster, Not Us
summary: Lobbyists for major technology companies capitalized on public outrage over Ticketmaster's handling of Taylor Swift concert tickets to deflect congressional antitrust scrutiny away from Big Tech. They argued that Congress should focus on clear monopolies like Ticketmaster, implying that existing antitrust laws are sufficient and that efforts to reform them to target tech giants are misguided. This strategy led to a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing focusing on Live Nation/Ticketmaster's monopolistic practices instead of Big Tech.

title: AST SpaceMobile raises $75 million, partners with TIM Brasil
summary: AST SpaceMobile has raised $75 million through an offering of Class A Common Stock and formed a partnership with Brazilian telco TIM Brasil. The funds will support the production and launch of the company's commercial satellites, while the partnership will enable TIM Brasil to test AST SpaceMobile's satellite-based 4G services in remote Brazilian locations. This move highlights AST SpaceMobile's mission to connect unserved areas and positions it alongside other companies in the growing satellite-to-phone connectivity market.

title: IBM Is Tech’s Most Beaten-Down Company
summary: This article argues that IBM has significantly fallen from its former prominence, ranking 49th on the Fortune 500 compared to 8th in 1980. Its recent financial results show flat revenue and modest net income, trailing far behind other tech giants like Apple, Amazon, and Microsoft. The author criticizes IBM for missing key technological advancements such as cloud computing, search, e-commerce, and operating systems despite its past R&D capabilities.

title: Is Augmented Reality safe?
summary: Augmented Reality (AR) blends digital information with the real world, raising significant safety concerns despite its benefits. The article highlights potential dangers in privacy, security, and mental health, including data collection, cyber-attacks, and the addictive nature of AR. It emphasizes the need for careful consideration and control as AR technology becomes more integrated into daily life.

title: Save $200 on the Sonos Arc Soundbar, now $699 (lowest price ever)
summary: The Sonos Arc Soundbar is currently available for $699, a $200 discount that marks its lowest recorded price, even beating Black Friday deals. This offer from Adorama applies to the white model and is for a limited time. The soundbar was rated 4.5 out of 5 in a hands-on review for its rich sound, substantial bass, and Dolby Atmos support.

title: Google continued to ramp up federal lobbying spending before DOJ filed second antitrust lawsuit
summary: Google's parent company, Alphabet, significantly increased its federal lobbying expenditures, spending over $13 million in 2022, prior to the Department of Justice filing its second antitrust lawsuit. The lawsuit alleges Google monopolized the digital advertising technology sector by acquiring rivals and manipulating the auction process to stifle competition. Despite these lobbying efforts and substantial political contributions, particularly to Democratic candidates, Alphabet also announced mass layoffs of 12,000 employees in January 2023.

title: Apple takes first steps towards 'Made in India' AirPods
summary: Apple has begun manufacturing components for its AirPods in India, marking a significant step towards the "Made in India" initiative for its products beyond the iPhone. Jabil Inc, an Apple supplier, is producing AirPods enclosures in Pune, India, and shipping them to China and Vietnam for assembly. This move is part of Apple's broader strategy to reduce its reliance on Chinese manufacturing and diversify its supply chain.

title: ‘Acapulco’ Renewed for Season 3 at Apple
summary: Apple has renewed its series "Acapulco" for a third season, which will consist of 10 episodes and begin production in the spring. The show stars Eugenio Derbez and is inspired by the film "How to Be A Latin Lover." The cast includes Enrique Arrizon, Fernando Carsa, Damián Alcázar, and others, continuing the story of Máximo Gallardo at a resort in 1985 and his older self in the present day.

title: Get Your Game on With Build-a-Bear's New 'Ted Lasso' Collection
summary: Build-A-Bear has launched a new collection of plush toys inspired by Apple TV+'s hit series, "Ted Lasso." The collection features a Coach Lasso bear, complete with team kit and mustache, along with accessories like aviator sunglasses and a Union Jack mug. Fans can also find AFC Richmond accessories to dress up other cuddly toys as they eagerly await the third season of the Emmy-winning show.

title: Exxon Vaults to Record Annual Profit of $55.7 Billion
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. achieved a record annual profit of $55.7 billion in 2022, marking a significant recovery after suffering losses during the pandemic and a historic proxy fight in 2021. This surge was primarily driven by soaring oil and gas prices globally, allowing Exxon to surpass most major companies in profitability, except for Apple and Microsoft. The company's resurgence reflects a turnaround in its financial performance and market standing.

title: Apple workplace rules violate U.S. labor law, agency finds
summary: A U.S. labor agency has found that Apple Inc. maintains workplace policies that unlawfully discourage employees from discussing working conditions. The National Labor Relations Board plans to issue a complaint unless Apple settles, citing policies around confidentiality and surveillance, and past comments from CEO Tim Cook that allegedly stymied worker organizing. Former Apple senior engineering manager Ashley Gjovik filed the initial complaints in 2021, and the NLRB investigates such charges.

title: Netflix Inc. stock rises Tuesday, still underperforms market
summary: Netflix Inc. stock saw a modest increase of 0.21% on Tuesday, closing at $353.86, despite a strong day for the broader market with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones also rising. The stock's performance underperformed compared to competitors like Apple, Walt Disney, and Comcast, and it remained significantly below its 52-week high. Trading volume was also notably lower than its 50-day average.

title: Spotify Reports Q4 2022 Earnings: Strong User Growth and Widened Losses
summary: Spotify reported strong Q4 2022 earnings, with revenue up 18% year-over-year to 3.17 billion euros ($3.43 billion) and monthly active users increasing by 20% to 489 million. However, the company's losses widened significantly due to higher personnel and advertising costs, leading to a planned 6% reduction in headcount. For Q1 2023, Spotify expects continued revenue growth and user base expansion, aiming for 500 million monthly active users, but anticipates an operating loss.

title: Apple Is Dropping Industrial Design Chief Role in Post-Jony Ive Era
summary: Apple Inc. will not replace its departing industrial design chief, Evans Hankey, signifying a major shift in the company's approach to product design after the departure of Jony Ive. Instead, the core industrial design team will report directly to Chief Operating Officer Jeff Williams, and veteran designers will be given expanded roles. This decision centralizes design under operations and elevates Williams, seen as a potential successor to CEO Tim Cook, while also acknowledging the challenge of finding a suitable replacement given recent departures from the design team.

title: McDonald’s new strategy to bring renewable energy to its supply chain
summary: McDonald's has launched a new strategy to decarbonize its supply chain by signing a 189-megawatt virtual power purchase agreement (VPPA) with its five logistics partners. This deal marks the first time a corporation has acted as an anchor buyer for an aggregation deal explicitly for its suppliers, simplifying access to renewable energy for smaller companies. The initiative targets Scope 3 emissions, specifically the electricity load of its logistics supply chain in the U.S., aligning with a growing trend of corporations providing resources to help suppliers transition to clean energy.

title: Samsung’s next frontier: XR in partnership with Qualcomm, Google
summary: Samsung Electronics is partnering with Qualcomm Technologies and Google LLC to enter the extended reality (XR) device market, which is projected to reach $1.39 trillion by 2030. This collaboration aims to challenge other Big Tech firms like Meta and Apple in the rapidly growing XR space. Although specific product details were not revealed, industry watchers expect Samsung to develop XR headsets utilizing Qualcomm's chipsets and Google's Android operating system, leveraging their existing smartphone collaboration.

title: Apple sales drop 5% in largest quarterly revenue decline since 2016
summary: Apple recorded its first year-over-year sales decline since 2019, with overall sales for the holiday quarter down 5%. CEO Tim Cook attributed this miss to a strong dollar, production issues in China affecting the iPhone 14 Pro and Pro Max, and the challenging macroeconomic environment. While iPhone and Mac sales decreased, the company saw a significant increase in iPad revenue and a 6% growth in its services business.

title: Apple Q1 2023 Revenues Slowed by Exchange Rates, COVID, and Inflation
summary: Apple's Q1 2023 financial results showed a revenue decrease of 5% and a profit decrease of 13.3% compared to the previous year, marking only the second such decline in a decade. CEO Tim Cook attributed this to foreign exchange headwinds, COVID-19 related production constraints impacting iPhone 14 Pro models, and a challenging macroeconomic environment. Despite these challenges, Apple reported strong performance in Services and iPad sales, reached 2 billion active devices globally, and avoided major layoffs seen in other tech giants.

title: Meta从虚拟元宇宙重回现实
summary: Meta Platforms reported a mixed Q4 2022 earnings, with revenue declining year-over-year but exceeding market expectations, driven by its traditional advertising business. While net income continued to decrease, particularly due to metaverse investments in Reality Labs, the company saw growth in its user base across its platforms. Meta is now signaling a return to prioritizing its core app business and cost-cutting measures, shifting focus from its aggressive metaverse push.

title: Peloton Rival Zwift Bets on Hardcore Racing In Your Living Room
summary: Zwift Inc., an exercise app with backing from KKR, specializes in virtual cycling races, gaining popularity among avid cyclists and investors. During the pandemic, it notably provided a virtual version of the Tour de France. The platform allows users to connect their bikes to virtual worlds for training or competition from home.

title: Corning Inc. recently cut about 1,500 jobs worldwide
summary: Corning Inc. recently announced a workforce reduction of approximately 1,500 jobs worldwide in mid-January due to macroeconomic concerns. This cut impacts less than 2.5% of its global employees. The announcement came as the company released its fourth-quarter and full-year 2022 financial results, reporting core sales growth but anticipating a sales decline in the first quarter of 2023 partly due to COVID-19 disruptions in China.

title: NLRB: Apple illegally interfered with employees’ protected activity
summary: The National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) has found merit in five charges against Apple, alleging the company violated the National Labor Relations Act by interfering with employees' protected activities. The charges include violations related to work rules, handbook rules, confidentiality policies, and specific statements and conduct by high-level executives that "reasonably tend to interfere with, restrain, or coerce employees in the exercise of their right to protected concerted activity." If Apple and the charging parties do not settle, the NLRB's regional director will issue a complaint and pursue the charges before an administrative law judge.

title: Purifying the ‘miracle metal’: How to decarbonize aluminium
summary: Aluminium, despite its versatility and recyclability, is incredibly energy-intensive to produce, contributing 2% of global man-made emissions. This article explores how a combination of renewable energy, new technologies like inert anodes and carbon capture, and extensive recycling can significantly reduce the carbon footprint of aluminium production. It also highlights the crucial role of coalitions like the First Movers Coalition and government support to overcome economic and supply chain challenges in achieving near-zero emissions.

title: Sonos Is Having a Secret Sale Ahead of President's Day
summary: Sonos is holding a "secret sale" on its popular speakers and soundbars ahead of President's Day and the Super Bowl, offering significant discounts. Highlighting the rarity of Sonos sales and their premium status, the article details deals on products like the Sonos Arc and Sonos Beam Gen 2, recommending them for home theater upgrades. The sale includes individual speakers and immersive sets, but the duration and inventory are limited.

title: Calamos Investments Launches New Sustainable Equities ETF SROI
summary: Calamos Investments has launched the Calamos Antetokounmpo Global Sustainable Equities ETF (SROI) on NYSE ARCA, in collaboration with NBA star Giannis Antetokounmpo. This actively managed ETF aims for long-term capital appreciation by investing in quality growth companies that integrate ESG principles, utilizing both traditional financial and nonfinancial indicators. The fund will also donate a portion of its profits to charity, reflecting a commitment to community impact.

title: 元宇宙烧了 137 亿美元，还得 Facebook 救 Meta
summary: Meta Platforms reported a Q4 2022 earnings beat, with its stock surging 23% despite a $13.7 billion loss in its metaverse division Reality Labs for the full year. The unexpected positive market reaction is attributed to lower investor expectations, positive signals from management regarding social advertising, and a $40 billion share buyback program. While the metaverse remains a long-term goal, Meta's immediate focus is on optimizing its core Facebook platform, pursuing short-video growth, and leveraging AI for advertising, coupled with significant cost-cutting measures including layoffs.

title: BioSig Appoints Steve Buhaly as CFO
summary: BioSig Technologies, Inc. has announced the retirement of its long-serving CFO, Steve Chaussy, after 12 years of service. Steve Buhaly, with 15 years of public company CFO experience, including a significant tenure at Qorvo, has been appointed as his successor. Buhaly's expertise in financial leadership, corporate expansion, and value creation is expected to support BioSig's commercial rollout of its PURE EP™ System and national scaling efforts.

title: Mobile App Development market, it is estimated to increase at the rate of more than 23.80% from 2020 to the end of the year 2030
summary: The global mobile app development market is projected to reach approximately USD 366.93 billion by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 23.80% from 2022 to 2030. This growth is driven by the increasing use of smartphones and other gadgets, the leveraging of mobile applications by e-commerce and social media platforms, and the declining cost of data services coupled with rising internet penetration. North America is expected to generate the highest revenues, while the Asia Pacific region is anticipated to show the highest CAGR.

title: Apple Stock Versus Microsoft Stock: Which Is the Better Buy Now?
summary: This article analyzes whether Apple or Microsoft is the better stock to buy based on Morningstar's metrics, including price/fair value, uncertainty, economic moat, and capital allocation. While both companies are giants facing economic headwinds, Morningstar finds Microsoft stock to be more attractive due to it being 17% undervalued with a lower uncertainty rating, earning it a 4-star rating compared to Apple's 3-star rating. Both companies have wide economic moats and exemplary capital allocation.

title: Exclusive: Hearing startup Tuned adds more employers with fresh funds
summary: Hearing startup Tuned has successfully raised $3.5 million in a seed extension round, bringing their total seed funding to $6 million. This new investment, led by Distributed Ventures, will fuel the expansion of Tuned's commercial team and its goal to position hearing support as a vital component of employee health benefits. The company also announced new leadership additions and plans to launch a pediatric vertical while continuing to target employers with its tech-agnostic hearing solutions.

title: AMD wins nearly a third of processor market, Arm's climb slows: analyst report
summary: AMD has significantly increased its market share in central processor units, capturing nearly a third of the x86 processor market from Intel, according to a recent analyst report from Mercury Research. This growth occurred during the worst PC chip market downturn since the 1980s. Meanwhile, Arm's rise in the PC market, primarily driven by Apple's Mac computers, slowed in the fourth quarter of 2022.

title: Cartões Bradesco seguem pontuando em compras com Apple Pay
summary: Bradesco credit card holders were concerned about a recent change in the bank's loyalty program regulations indicating that transactions made through digital wallets would no longer accrue points. However, MacMagazine clarified with Bradesco that NFC payment services like Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Samsung Pay, as well as PayPal, will continue to be eligible for point accumulation. The new rules, which exclude app-based payment platforms like PicPay and Mercado Pago, will take effect on March 6th.

title: Navigate 2023 With Recession-Resistant ETF ZECP
summary: The Zacks Earnings Consistent Portfolio ETF (ZECP) is presented as a recession-resistant strategy for investors concerned about a potential economic downturn in 2023. ZECP, Zacks Investment Management's first ETF, identifies companies with strong balance sheets and consistent earnings, having demonstrated resilience through past recessions. The fund seeks to offer an active approach to navigate market volatility, focusing on quality companies with stable historic and forecasted earnings per share.

title: Apple hires its first Chief People Officer in executive reshuffle
summary: Apple has appointed Carol Surface as its first chief people officer, a move that shifts human resources responsibilities from retail chief Deirdre O'Brien. Surface, previously with Medtronic Plc, will report directly to CEO Tim Cook and oversee Apple’s 164,000 employees. This reshuffle aims to give more prominence to the HR role and allow O'Brien to focus more fully on Apple's expanding and increasingly challenging retail operations.

title: Wall Street ends sharply higher as investors eye inflation data
summary: Wall Street closed sharply higher as investors awaited key inflation data, which is expected to influence the Federal Reserve's future interest rate decisions. Tech-related heavyweights, including Meta Platforms, Microsoft, Nvidia, Apple, and Amazon, significantly contributed to the S&P 500's gains, with Meta jumping after news of potential further layoffs. Fidelity National Information Services slumped after announcing a spinoff of its merchant payments business.

title: T-Mobile suffers major network outage across US
summary: T-Mobile experienced a significant network outage across the United States on Monday night, affecting thousands of customers who reported issues with calls, texts, and data. The disruption, which coincided with network chief Neville Ray's retirement announcement, was attributed to a "third-party fiber interruption." Although the carrier seemed to be resolving the issue by late evening, customers were frustrated by the service interruption.

title: These Stocks Are Leading the Growth Rebound
summary: Growth stocks, particularly in the tech sector, have seen a significant rebound in early 2023 after a difficult 2022, outperforming value stocks. This surge is likely driven by investor expectations that the Federal Reserve may soon pause interest rate hikes. Despite strong recent gains, the Morningstar US Growth Index still needs a substantial rally to recover fully from last year's losses.

title: Qualcomm introduces new Snapdragon X75 mobile modem chip
summary: Qualcomm has unveiled its new Snapdragon X75 5G modem chip, expected to power future flagship smartphones. This new chip features an enhanced AI processor that is 2.5 times faster than its predecessor, designed to optimize 5G connections and consider sensory data for improved performance. The Snapdragon X75 also supports 5G Advanced and Qualcomm Satellite technology, aiming to reduce hardware costs, improve internet coverage, and enable satellite connectivity for handsets.

title: Microsoft Now Supporting Windows Virtualization on Mac M1, M2, via Parallels Desktop 18
summary: Microsoft has officially announced full support for running Windows 11 virtually on Apple Mac Silicon-powered computers (M1, M2, Pro, Ultra chips) via Alludo's Parallels Desktop 18. This integration offers Mac users a legitimate and hassle-free way to operate Windows 11 without requiring hard drive partitioning. Users can purchase or subscribe to Parallels Desktop for Mac to enable this functionality.

title: Forget Milk and Eggs: Supermarkets Are Having a Fire Sale on Data About You
summary: Supermarkets like Kroger are making significant profits by collecting and selling extensive data on their customers' purchasing habits and personal information to brands and advertisers. This data, which includes demographics, financial information, and even in-store movements, is enriched with third-party data and used for targeted advertising. The proposed merger between Kroger and Albertsons would significantly expand this data pool, raising privacy concerns among regulators and lawmakers.

title: Exclusive: SoftBank's Arm China profit drops over 90% in 2022
summary: Arm China, a joint venture of SoftBank's Arm Ltd, experienced a more than 90% drop in net profit in 2022, falling to $3.2 million despite a significant revenue increase to nearly $890 million. This decline occurred during the first year of new management appointed by SoftBank, following a two-year battle to oust the previous CEO. The profit slump is attributed in part to a $37 million loss in foreign exchange, though it reportedly will not impact Arm Ltd's overall financial performance as its royalty and licensing fees come before profit calculation.

title: UBS recommends its clients grab a full serving of Buffett's incredible, UNDERVALUED Berkshire Hathaway
summary: UBS is recommending its clients buy shares of Berkshire Hathaway (BRK), considering it undervalued by over 20% compared to its intrinsic value. The article highlights BRK's strong performance during past recessions, its diverse business mix, robust balance sheet, and substantial liquidity as reasons for its potential to outperform in an uncertain economic outlook. It also notes Buffett's historically aggressive share buybacks when the stock trades at such discounts and details recent portfolio moves, including the sale of Taiwan Semi shares and the success of BYD investments.

title: Groupon Outsources Legal Executive Role to Winston & Strawn (1)
summary: Groupon's general counsel, Dane Drobny, is stepping down next week to rejoin Winston & Strawn as a partner. Drobny will continue to serve as Groupon's outside general counsel through the end of the year, as the company undergoes restructuring and workforce reductions. His departure follows two rounds of layoffs at the e-commerce marketplace.

title: Garmin Ltd. stock outperforms competitors despite losses on the day

Despite the overall market's mixed performance and Garmin's losses, the stock outperformed competitors like Apple Inc. (AAPL) and Alphabet Inc. (GOOG, GOOGL) which saw larger drops. The trading volume for Garmin exceeded its 50-day average.

title: Familiar Faces Powering Growth Stock Resurgence
summary: Growth stocks are experiencing a resurgence in early 2023, primarily driven by large- and mega-cap names like Apple, Amazon, and Tesla, according to Morningstar research. This trend is significantly boosting ETFs such as the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) and the Invesco NASDAQ 100 ETF (QQQM). The rally is further supported by the strong performance of tech sectors like software infrastructure, software applications, and semiconductors, alongside investor optimism that the Federal Reserve may soon conclude its interest rate hikes, potentially averting a recession.

title: Trump’s Truth Social Dilemma
summary: This article examines Donald Trump's dilemma regarding his social media platform, Truth Social, one year after its launch. Despite having his Twitter and Meta accounts reinstated, Trump primarily uses Truth Social, but faces pressure to return to mainstream platforms for his 2024 presidential campaign's reach and fundraising, potentially impacting Truth Social's viability and his exclusivity deal.

title: Major League Soccer and RBC Wealth Management Announce Multi-Year Partnership
summary: Major League Soccer (MLS) and RBC Wealth Management have partnered in a multi-year deal aimed at engaging MLS's diverse fanbase and raising the profile of soccer in the lead-up to the 2026 World Cup. The partnership will include RBC Wealth Management's presence at MLS Player Engagement events, brand integration across various platforms, and a joint initiative with MLS WORKS to support the U.S. Soccer Foundation’s Soccer for Success program for approximately 500 children annually. This collaboration seeks to help RBC Wealth Management expand its business and connect with a new generation of investors while growing the game and strengthening community impact.

title: Apple HomePod 2 vs Sonos One: is it worth paying more?
summary: This article compares the Apple HomePod 2 and the Sonos One smart speakers, evaluating their price, design, sound quality, and smart features. While the HomePod 2 is significantly more expensive, the review concludes it offers superior performance and a more premium experience, especially for users integrated into the Apple ecosystem. The Sonos One remains a strong contender for those outside the Apple ecosystem or looking for a more affordable option.

title: Microsoft teams up with Nvidia and Nintendo in 10-year deal to stream Xbox games
summary: Microsoft has secured 10-year agreements with Nvidia and Nintendo to stream Xbox games as part of its strategy to address antitrust concerns regarding its proposed acquisition of Activision Blizzard. This partnership aims to make Xbox and potential Activision titles available on Nvidia's GeForce Now cloud gaming service and Nintendo platforms, covering various devices. The move is intended to placate regulators scrutinizing the $69 billion deal.

title: AMD Puts Hopes on Packaging, Memory on Logic, Optical Comms for Decade Ahead
summary: AMD outlined its decade-long strategy for continued performance and efficiency gains in computing at ISSCC 2023. The company aims to overcome tapering process technology benefits through advanced architecture, packaging technologies like 3D CPU & GPU silicon, and tighter integration of compute and memory, including processing-in-memory solutions. Additionally, AMD plans to leverage optical communications integrated with compute dies for efficiency boosts, continuing its fierce competition in the semiconductor industry with ever faster and more efficient chips.

title: Dexcom G6 Continuous Glucose Monitoring System Launches in Singapore
summary: Dexcom, Inc. has officially launched its G6 Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) System in Singapore for individuals aged two and older, including pregnant women. This system eliminates the need for routine fingersticks by continuously measuring and wirelessly sending glucose levels to a receiver or compatible smart device, offering real-time data and customizable alerts. The launch marks Dexcom's first CGM availability in Southeast Asia, with DKSH Singapore Pte Ltd appointed as the sales, marketing, and distribution service provider.

While the integration of productivity apps like Zoom caters to professionals, the inclusion of TikTok and games like Angry Birds also allows for entertainment during stationary periods.

Apple Financing LLC, a subsidiary of Apple Inc., is responsible for credit assessment and lending, and will report loans to U.S. credit bureaus starting in the fall, while Mastercard and Goldman Sachs facilitate the program.

This move has already impacted competitors' stock, with Apple directly underwriting, funding, and collecting on the loans.

This initiative is part of Apple's broader commitment to eventually make all products with only recycled and renewable materials and achieve carbon neutrality by 2030.

title: Big Tech Illegally Uses NDAs to Silence Would-Be-Whistleblowers, SEC Tips Allege
summary: The SEC has received whistleblower tips alleging that major tech companies, including an Apple Inc. subcontractor, Electronic Arts Inc., and Block Inc., are using illegally restrictive non-disclosure agreements (NDAs). These NDAs reportedly forbid employees from reporting misconduct to the SEC, in violation of Rule 21F-17 of the SEC Whistleblower Program. The law firm Kohn, Kohn & Colapinto LLP filed these complaints, highlighting a perceived willful disregard for the law given previous SEC enforcement actions against such agreements.

Other conditions, like providing affordable childcare and restrictions on expanding manufacturing in "countries of concern" such as China, also pose challenges for chipmakers.

title: Semiconductor industry electricity consumption to more than double by 2030: study
summary: A Greenpeace East Asia report projects that global semiconductor manufacturing will consume 237 terawatt hours of electricity by 2030, more than doubling current levels and equating to Australia's 2021 electricity consumption. This energy-intensive industry, critical to the tech supply chain, is also set to emit 86 million tonnes of CO2e by 2030, exceeding Portugal's 2021 total emissions. The report criticizes major manufacturers like Samsung and TSMC for their reliance on fossil fuels and lack of ambitious 100% renewable energy commitments by 2030, urging them to accelerate renewable energy development in East Asia.

title: PayPal and Venmo users shouldn't store money on the apps long term
summary: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) has warned users against storing money long-term on payment apps like PayPal, Venmo, and CashApp, citing potential risks during a financial crisis. While some specific features like PayPal Savings or Apple Cash with identity verification may offer insurance, the default accounts typically do not.

title: Spotlight on illegal hiring practices: Apple pays $25M for recruiting, job ad mistakes
summary: Apple Inc. has agreed to pay $25 million to settle allegations of illegal hiring practices related to its PERM program. A DOJ investigation found Apple failed to recruit U.S. citizens or green card holders, did not advertise these positions on its external website, and required paper applications for PERM jobs while allowing electronic applications for others. The settlement includes $18.25 million for discrimination victims and $6.75 million for civil penalties, with Apple also agreeing to revise its recruitment practices and provide employee training.

title: FMR LLC Bolsters Portfolio with Fidelity International Value Fac
summary: FMR LLC, also known as Fidelity, has significantly expanded its investment portfolio by acquiring 350,126 shares of the Fidelity International Value Factor ETF (FIVA) at $21.95 per share. This transaction, executed on October 31, 2023, increases FMR LLC's holdings in FIVA to 1,099,261 shares, representing a 32.33% position in its portfolio. The move reflects Fidelity's strategic investment in an ETF that has shown a 9.1% year-to-date performance.

title: FMR LLC Acquires New Stake in Magenta Therapeutics Inc
summary: FMR LLC, through its flagship company Fidelity Investments, has acquired a new stake in Magenta Therapeutics Inc (MGTA) by purchasing 2,218,212 shares at $0.6996 per share. This transaction gives FMR LLC a 14.97% ownership stake in the clinical-stage biotechnology company, indicating a strategic investment aligning with the firm's focus on technology and healthcare sectors. Despite Magenta Therapeutics currently operating at a loss, FMR LLC's move suggests a belief in the company's long-term value and transformative potential in stem cell and gene therapy.

title: FMR LLC Bolsters Position in Fidelity Low Volatility Factor ETF
summary: FMR LLC (Fidelity) has increased its holdings in the Fidelity Low Volatility Factor ETF (FDLO) by acquiring an additional 892,483 shares on October 31, 2023. This strategic move brings their total ownership in FDLO to 19.61%, reflecting confidence in the ETF's strong performance and growth potential. The transaction aligns with FMR LLC's growth-oriented investment philosophy and diversifies their extensive portfolio, which includes major tech holdings like Apple, Amazon, and Microsoft.

title: Tepper’s Appaloosa dumps Apple stake and loads up on Amazon’s stock
summary: David Tepper’s Appaloosa hedge fund significantly increased its stake in Amazon.com Inc. and completely divested its position in Apple Inc. during the last quarter. The fund also raised its holdings in Google parent Alphabet Inc. and Facebook parent Meta Platforms Inc., as detailed in a recent SEC filing. This move indicates a shift in Tepper's portfolio allocation towards these tech giants.

title: What's next for satellite communications on Android?
summary: Apple has extended its Emergency SOS via satellite service for iPhone 14 and 15 users to two years, while Qualcomm's Snapdragon Satellite initiative for Android has failed due to lack of OEM integration. This leaves Iridium, a key satellite provider, free to pursue new partnerships directly with smartphone makers. The future of satellite communication on Android is unclear, though Samsung is rumored to introduce a solution with the Galaxy S24, and current options include standalone devices like the Motorola Defy Sat Link and Garmin inReach Mini 2.

title: SIT Investment Associates Inc Adds DWS Municipal Income Trust to Its Portfolio
summary: SIT Investment Associates Inc has expanded its portfolio by acquiring 567,353 shares of DWS Municipal Income Trust (KTF) on November 15, 2023, for $8.23 per share, increasing its total holdings in KTF to 4,433,361 shares. This strategic investment in the tax-exempt securities focused company now constitutes 11.32% of SIT Investment Associates Inc's portfolio, despite KTF's challenging financial health, including negative ROE and ROA, and a low GF Score of 37/100. The move by the reputable investment management firm, known for its diverse investment holdings, suggests potential long-term confidence in KTF's prospects, which value investors will monitor closely.

title: Warren Buffet's latest buys and sells
summary: This article details Berkshire Hathaway's latest stock buys and sells from its third-quarter 2023 13F filing, highlighting that the company was a net seller despite a tough market quarter, leading to a record cash stake. It identifies three undervalued Warren Buffett stocks within Berkshire Hathaway’s portfolio—Bank of America, American Express, and Kraft Heinz—providing Morningstar's analysis and key metrics for each. The piece also lists the stocks Berkshire Hathaway sold entirely, including Activision Blizzard, Celanese, General Motors, Johnson & Johnson, Mondelez International, Procter & Gamble, and United Parcel Service, while noting a significant reduction in its Chevron holdings.

title: Unity 6 debuts next year with AI-powered innovations and platform updates
summary: Unity announced its upcoming Unity 6 platform, set to launch in 2024, featuring significant AI innovations and platform updates. Key announcements from the Unite conference include the early access of Unity Muse for content creation, a preview of Unity 6, and the introduction of Unity Cloud. These updates aim to address developer feedback and enhance the game development process following recent controversies over pricing changes.

title: Warren Buffett Has Bought Shares of This Stock for 21 Consecutive Quarters -- and It's Not Apple
summary: Warren Buffett has consistently invested in Berkshire Hathaway's own stock for 21 consecutive quarters, authorizing over $72 billion in repurchases since mid-2018. This strategy, enabled by a change in buyback clauses, aims to reward long-term shareholders by increasing their ownership stakes and potentially boosting earnings per share. While Apple constitutes nearly half of Berkshire's invested assets, the frequent repurchase of Berkshire Hathaway shares itself highlights Buffett's conviction in his own company.

title: AT&T’s Black Friday Deals on the iPhone 15 Pro & More
summary: AT&T announced its Black Friday deals for the holiday season, offering significant savings on various Apple products including the iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15, iPhone 14, iPhone 14 Pro, iPhone SE 3rd Gen, iPad, and Apple Watch. Deals include trade-in options, no trade-in required offers, and low monthly payments, catering to both new and existing customers. Additionally, AT&T highlighted benefits like flexible shopping, unlimited plans with 5G access, AT&T Fiber deals, and special discounts for military, veterans, teachers, nurses, and physicians.

title: Network of Lies review: Brian Stelter on Fox News, Trump and Dominion
summary: Brian Stelter's book "Network of Lies" examines Fox News's role in spreading election conspiracies following the 2020 election, leading to significant legal and financial repercussions, such as the Dominion settlement. The review highlights Rupert Murdoch's recent step down, the Murdochs' balancing act of profitability and audience satisfaction, and the ongoing influence of Donald Trump on the network and Republican politics. Despite the controversies, the article suggests little change is expected from Fox News as it navigates complex defamation lawsuits and competitive political landscapes.

title: Apple’s In-House Technologies Team Still Has Plenty of Work to Do
summary: This article discusses Apple's intensive efforts to design and manufacture its own core hardware components, such as cameras, screens, modems, and batteries, for its products. It also touches on Apple's adoption of the RCS texting standard, the revelation of its revenue share from the Google search deal, and a key health executive's move to Oura. The piece highlights that Apple's in-house technologies team has extensive work ahead in its strategic initiative to control major parts of its devices.

title: Venmo, Cash App users sue Apple over peer-to-peer payment fees
summary: Venmo and Cash App customers have filed a proposed class-action lawsuit against Apple Inc. alleging the company abused its market power in mobile peer-to-peer payments, leading to "rapidly inflating prices." The lawsuit claims Apple's agreements with PayPal's Venmo and Block's Cash App violate U.S. antitrust law by limiting "feature competition," including prohibiting decentralized cryptocurrency technology. This case adds to Apple's ongoing antitrust legal challenges, seeking an injunction that could force Apple to divest or segregate its Apple Cash business.

title: Should You Buy the Invesco QQQ ETF With the Nasdaq At An All-Time High? History Offers a Clear Answer.
summary: This article discusses the Invesco QQQ ETF and whether it's a good investment despite the Nasdaq Composite being at an all-time high. It analyzes historical data of the Nasdaq's performance after reaching new highs, suggesting that further gains are common. The article concludes that dollar-cost averaging into QQQ is a sensible strategy regardless of market highs, as it tracks the Nasdaq 100 which tends to rise over time.

title: Gaming Industry Charts a Rebound in 2023
summary: The gaming industry is experiencing a significant rebound in 2023 driven by strong console sales, new game releases, and innovations in mobile and cloud gaming. This recovery, following a dip in 2022, is further supported by anticipation of increased M&A activity and strategic moves by major players like Microsoft, Apple, and Netflix, positioning the sector for continued growth into 2024. The article highlights strong U.S. sales, hardware as a primary catalyst, and key factors like M&A and technological advancements shaping the industry's future trajectory.

title: Sonos Readies $400-Plus Headphones to Rival Apple and Bose, TV Set-Top Box
summary: Sonos Inc. is planning a significant expansion into new product categories, including headphones priced over $400 and a TV set-top box. These new offerings are expected to compete with products from Apple, Bose, and Roku, marking a strategic move beyond its traditional smart speakers and sound bars. The headphones could launch as early as April, with the set-top box following by the end of 2024.

title: InterDigital’s Alain Mourad Elected Chair of New ETSI Industry Specification Group on Integrated Sensing and Communications
summary: Dr. Alain Mourad, Head of InterDigital’s Wireless Lab Europe, has been elected Chair of the newly formed ETSI Industry Specification Group (ISG) on Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC). This group aims to establish the technical foundation for ISAC technology and its standardization in 6G, defining use cases and developing evaluation roadmaps. The ISG will also study privacy, security, and sustainability aspects of ISAC within the 6G framework.

title: Department of Justice and Apple Reach $25 Million Landmark Agreement
summary: The U.S. Department of Justice announced a $25 million agreement with Apple Inc. to resolve allegations of discriminatory hiring practices related to the permanent labor certification (PERM) program. Apple's recruitment practices for PERM positions, which included not advertising on its public-facing career website and requiring mailed paper applications, deterred U.S. workers. The settlement includes $6.75 million in civil penalties and $18.25 million for a backpay fund for victims, and mandates Apple to align PERM recruitment with its standard practices.

title: OpenAI Says Sam Altman to Return as CEO in Dramatic Reversal
summary: Sam Altman is set to return as CEO of OpenAI after being ousted less than a week prior, following intense negotiations and pressure from investors like Microsoft and nearly all of the company's employees. The agreement includes a new initial board of directors led by Bret Taylor, with Larry Summers and Adam D’Angelo, and an internal investigation into the conduct that led to Altman's dismissal. This dramatic reversal comes after widespread calls for Altman's reinstatement and highlights the significant influence of investors and employees on the future of the AI startup.

title: Warren Buffett-Led Berkshire Hathaway Sells Its Entire Procter & Gamble Stake. Should You?
summary: Berkshire Hathaway fully exited its small position in Procter & Gamble, likely due to consolidating its portfolio and P&G's premium valuation compared to other opportunities like Apple. Despite Berkshire's sale, P&G is still considered a worthwhile investment for risk-averse individuals due to its strong brand development, pricing power, and commitment to shareholder returns through dividends and buybacks. The article suggests that while P&G's valuation is high, its other characteristics make it a solid choice for passive income and portfolio stability.

title: Sonos is reportedly working on a streaming video TV set top box, along with headphones
summary: Sonos is reportedly expanding its product line beyond speakers and soundbars. The company isSaid to be working on over-the-ear headphones for a March 2024 launch, possibly priced between $400 and $500, and high-end earbuds. Additionally, Sonos is reportedly developing an Android-based streaming video TV set-top box, codenamed "Pinewood," which could launch in late 2024 or early 2025.

title: Deere must face US farmers' 'right-to-repair' lawsuits, judge rules
summary: A U.S. judge has ruled that Deere & Co must face consolidated lawsuits from farmers accusing the agricultural machinery maker of unlawfully conspiring to restrict maintenance and repair services. The judge rejected Deere's arguments for dismissal, stating that the plaintiffs met the legal thresholds to pursue their antitrust claims. This case is part of a broader "right-to-repair" movement challenging restrictive repair practices across various industries.

title: Amkor Announces U.S. Advanced Packaging and Test Facility In Peoria
summary: Amkor Technology, Inc. announced a $2 billion investment to build an advanced packaging and test facility in Peoria, Arizona, creating 2,000 new jobs. This facility will be the largest outsourced advanced packaging facility in the US, bolstering America's national security and semiconductor supply chain. Apple will be the first and largest customer, and Amkor has applied for CHIPS funding to support the project.

title: $2 billion semiconductor testing and packaging facility planned for Peoria
summary: Amkor Technology Inc. plans to build a $2 billion semiconductor testing and advanced packaging facility in Peoria, Arizona, near the TSMC plant. This facility, expected to create 2,000 jobs, will test and package chips for Apple and aims to strengthen the domestic semiconductor supply chain. The project is seen as a crucial step for Arizona's semiconductor ecosystem and national security.

title: Apple announces expanded partnership with Amkor for advanced silicon packaging in the U.S.
summary: Apple announced an expanded partnership with Amkor, designating Apple as the first and largest customer for Amkor's new manufacturing and packaging facility in Peoria, Arizona. This facility will package Apple silicon produced at the nearby TSMC fab, strengthening Apple's commitment to American manufacturing. Amkor plans to invest approximately $2 billion in the project, creating over 2,000 jobs, as part of Apple's broader commitment to invest $430 billion in the U.S. economy.

summary: Apple Inc. bonds have generated equity-like returns for investors in the past month, with prices climbing as Treasury yields have tumbled. summary: Apple Inc. (AAPL) stock rose by 0.31% to $189.95 on Thursday, outperforming the mixed stock market session which saw the Dow Jones Industrial Average rise and the NASDAQ Composite Index fall. The company's shares closed $8.28 below their 52-week high.

summary: Apple announced it will be the primary customer for Amkor Technology Inc.'s new $2 billion chip packaging facility in Arizona, which will package chips produced by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) at a nearby complex. This facility will play a crucial role in assembling and protecting the next generation of processors for various Apple products. The investment underscores Apple's commitment to American manufacturing and will create over 2,000 jobs.

summary: Cognizant Technology Solutions announced layoffs impacting employees linked to Apple in Austin. The contractors affected will receive pay while exploring other positions within Cognizant. This move adds to a series of technology sector layoffs in Austin, though Central Texas is noted to be somewhat sheltered from broader industry cuts.

title: One ETF that focuses on employee happiness is outperforming the market this year
summary: An ETF focused on companies with high employee happiness, the Harbor Human Capital Factor U.S. Large Cap ETF (HAPI), has outperformed the S&P 500 this year, climbing nearly 25% compared to the benchmark's less than 20% gain. The fund's strategy is based on Irrational Capital's extensive employee surveys and publicly available data, creating a "human capital score" that is considered a novel and uncorrelated investment factor. While the large-cap HAPI fund includes major tech stocks contributing to its performance, a similar small-cap ETF (HAPS) is also available, offering potential for future growth.

title: Walmart stops advertising on X, adding to growing list of companies
summary: Walmart has ceased advertising on X, joining several other major companies like Apple, Disney, and IBM, citing that it found other platforms to better reach its customers. This decision was part of a gradual reduction in advertising on X, not a sudden halt, according to a source familiar with the situation and an X executive. The social media platform has faced a significant exodus of advertisers due to concerns over antisemitic content, exacerbated by recent controversies involving Elon Musk's comments and his subsequent strong reaction to advertisers.

The investment aims to bolster the US’s chipmaking capabilities, reduce reliance on foreign packaging capacity, and has applied for Chips Act funding.

title: Sonos roadmap reveals multiple audio launches intended in 2024
summary: Sonos is planning an "aggressive" roadmap of new audio products and software updates for 2024, including new in-ceiling speakers, headphones, a second-generation Roam, a high-end amplifier, and a high-end soundbar. A set-top box and subwoofer are also planned for late 2024 or 2025 releases. The company aims to revive sales through these launches, despite facing skepticism in competitive markets.

Analysts have speculated on several potential suitors for Apple's card partnership, including Amex, JPMorgan Chase, Synchrony Financial, Capital One, and Bread.

title: Who’s ready for a Gamestop mutual fund? Not this broker
